correctness.rationale: Every proper ideal lies in the radical of the local cube-zero algebra. Its projections U and W satisfy V⊗U+U⊗V⊆W, and quotienting by this exactly identified kernel gives the arbitrary B and linear graph lift φ. Conversely these data are always an ideal; the bijection is characteristic-free. Grassmannian and affine-bundle dimensions yield the complete Gaussian count. A dual Pluecker calculation identifies the four-ideal cone with three explicit prime Veronese quadrics, verifies its smooth charts and unique singular vertex, and counts its points. A direct complete finite subspace checker passes five cases (including two 7-dimensional algebra cases), but only corroborates the proof.

value.rationale: Exact ideal distributions across every number of free generators and every finite field are intrinsic structural invariants of the first nontrivial radical-layer extension. The free lift parameters are absent from radical-square-zero cases. The natural smallest two-generator four-ideal locus is a singular projective twisted-cubic cone with a sharp unique singular boundary while its finite-field count coincides with that of a projective plane; that geometric distinction is significant, not merely a numerical exercise.
